title: Packed quantized lane fusion and KV fastpath for transformer kernels
author: Avery Chen
description:
Context and motivation: production inference for quantized transformer models revealed two recurring hotspots: (1) scatter in kernel entrypoints when lanes have mixed quant formats (INT8 vs FP8) causing suboptimal vectorization and register pressure, and (2) KV-cache hits that still triggered a partial dequantize path because of legacy prefix handling. This PR implements a packed-lane fusion approach for Q/K/V and attention kernels plus a lightweight KV fastpath that avoids dequantizing cached keys under compatible quantization metadata.

What this PR does (high level): packed-lane fusion: introduces a small buffer-format and tiled iterator that packs lanes of compatible quant types into contiguous microtiles before calling a single vectorized microkernel. The microkernel is agnostic to whether input tiles are INT8 or FP8; it expects a per-lane scale table and emits a compact requantized output. This reduces branches at the kernel boundary and enables wider SIMD usage across mixed-precision model snapshots. KV fastpath: adds a compatibility check to the KV cache lookup pipeline. When a cached entry has identical quant metadata and contiguous layout, we return a pointer to the packed tile and skip the dequant->requant transform on the hot path. The fastpath is opt-in via a new model-config flag `kv.packed_fastpath=true` and protected behind a feature flag with rollout gating.

Key changes (files/modules): sources changed include runtime/submitter/continuous_batcher.cc (scheduling hooks to detect prefix reuse), runtime/kvcache/packed_cache.{cc,h} (cache metadata + packed tile allocator), kernels/quant_microkernel_vnni.S (vectorized kernel entry that consumes packed tiles), runtime/exec/kernel_dispatcher.cc (packed-lane dispatch path), and python/tests/regression/test_quant_kv_fastpath.py (behavioral tests). Several small config and CI test updates were added for stress runs.

Commits summary: - feat: packed-lane tile iterator and allocator - feat: quant microkernel (VNNI-optimized) with per-lane scale table - perf: KV cache fastpath and metadata checks - test: end-to-end regression + microbench harness - docs: rollout and feature-flag notes

Microbench results (CI perf harness): int8-legacy baseline (64 batch, 32 tokens): 1.00x throughput; packed-lane + fastpath: 1.34x throughput, 12% lower p95 latency on short contexts (<=16) due to avoided dequantize; mixed-int8/fp8 snapshots saw 1.18x improvement (reduced kernel entry overhead). Memory impact: packed tiles increase transient memory by ~6% but reduce copy-related allocations on hot paths.

Compatibility and rollout: new model-config flag `kv.packed_fastpath` defaults to false. Operators can enable per-deployment via runtime config. We ship with a safe fallback: if metadata mismatch is detected or the packed allocator cannot satisfy alignment, we fall back to the existing dequant path. The change is backwards-compatible with on-disk cache files: on startup we scan cache entries and mark which ones are eligible for fastpath.

Review highlights and decisions: - Diego requested an explicit invariants doc for per-lane scale tables; added comments and a short design note under docs/design/quant-packed-lane.md. - Priya asked to keep the fallback cheap; introduced a one-shot check and moved heavy consistency checks to background validation to avoid tail latency. - Sam asked about GPU scheduling interactions; added a dispatcher hint so CUDA/hip backends can prefer aligned buffers for packed tiles (no functional change).

Testing and CI: unit tests for allocator, microkernel correctness (bit-exact requant thresholds for fixed seeds), and regression tests for KV cache semantics were added. CI runs included microbench stress on a dedicated perf runner; initial flaky failure in the NV kernel checksum test was fixed by tightening rounding behavior in the microkernel. Final CI status: pass (linux-AMD64, linux-CUDA smoke, python-integration).

Security and observability: added a perf metric `kv.fastpath_hits` and `kv.fastpath_misses` and exposed a small debug endpoint to enumerate cached entries eligible for fastpath. No sensitive data is added to logs.

Docs and release notes: brief rollout instructions and the flag description were added to docs/ops/feature_flags.md and docs/perf/quant_optimizations.md.

Merge and follow-ups: merged with squash on 2026-03-02 after approvals. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-11002: improve cross-GPU pinned allocator for packed tiles, and ENG-11014: extend fastpath to multi-head grouped layouts.

Notes for maintainers: keep an eye on p95 latency in the first week after rollout for models with high prefix reuse and heterogeneous quant snapshots. If regressions occur, disable `kv.packed_fastpath` and collect the `kv.fastpath_*` metrics for triage.

release_notes: Improves quantized inference throughput for mixed INT8/FP8 models by packing compatible lanes and avoiding unnecessary dequant on KV cache hits. Opt-in via kv.packed_fastpath; safe fallback to legacy path. Metrics: kv.fastpath_hits / kv.fastpath_misses.
notes_for_backport: Not recommended for older release branches without the updated cache ABI and dispatcher changes; backport requires adding packed_cache.h and kernel dispatch hooks.
